thread:
amanda: small design spike idea for approval flow on eval scorecards — instead of a full modal, what if we do an inline micro-confirm for quick scans? e.g., click \"Approve\" -> row flips to tiny confirm bar: \"Are you sure? [Yes] [Undo]\" so the user can keep scanning

ryan: I like minimizing context switches. concern: accidental taps on mobile. micro-confirm needs a short delay or undo affordance.

leo: agree on undo. also need clear live region announcements: \"Scorecard approved. Undo available for 5s.\" so screen reader users know they can undo.

nina: copy bikeshed: \"Approve\" vs \"Mark as OK\". and for micro-confirm text: \"Approved — Undo\" vs \"Marked OK — Undo\". shorter is better for scan.

amanda: mobile handling: on small screens inline confirm could push list, might be jarring. maybe overlay a slim toast anchored to the row instead of flipping the row.

ryan: toast approach could work; ensure it's dismissible and keyboard-focusable. keyboard users should be able to Tab to the Undo button.

leo: accessibility checklist: 1) aria-live polite announce on approval with undo timer, 2) Undo is focusable and reachable with Tab, 3) Provide non-timeout fallback (e.g., history) for users who miss the timer, 4) high-contrast colors for confirm state, 5) prefer-reduced-motion respected.

nina: about accidental approvals: add an optional safety toggle in settings for \"Require confirm for approvals\". default off for power users, on for safety-critical teams.

amanda: good idea. also consider a small icon indicator for \"reversible action\" so users know it can be undone within N seconds. tiny question: what should N be? 5s? 10s?

ryan: 5s feels short for keyboard+screen reader users. recommend 8-10s to be safe. we'll test in accessibility pilot.

leo: implementation note: use a cancellable promise on the backend to mark the approval final after timer expires, or mark as pending with a TTL key. backend needs to support undo window.

nina: copy for undo toast: \"Marked OK. Undo\" (announce: \"Item marked OK. Undo available for 10 seconds\"). keep toast text concise but announce details.

amanda: UI nit: color for approved state — propose a neutral green with a check icon and label `Approved` to avoid cultural color assumptions. include visible text always, not just color.

ryan: also add an audit trail entry that shows \"Approved by X (undo allowed until HH:MM:SS)\" so we have visibility in case of mistakes.

leo: keyboard shortcuts: allow `Ctrl+Enter` to approve focused item, but respect settings where confirm is required. if confirm is on, shortcut should trigger the micro-confirm not finalize immediately.

nina: copy variant suggestion for confirmation UI: Variant A: \"Approve — Are you sure? [Yes] [Cancel]\"; Variant B (micro): \"Approved — Undo\" (with timer). I prefer B for speed.

amanda: we should run a small internal test: A/B micro vs modal for speed and error rate. add to launch checklist.

ryan: perf: avoid layout shift; prefer toast anchored with transform rather than DOM reflow. also respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and animate opacity only.

leo: QA tasks: keyboard navigation to micro-confirm, screen reader announcement accuracy, undo restores previous state including any tags/labels, mobile layout with soft keyboard open.

nina: legal/regulatory: for enterprise customers wanting immutable approvals, add a flag to disable undo and persist immediate finalization. document in admin settings.

amanda: next steps: I'll mock both micro-toast and modal flows, include copy variants and the 10s undo timer default. ryan will check with infra about TTL implementation. leo will draft accessibility QA checklist. nina will draft microcopy variants for product-review.

design-bot: ticket created: PRJ-4988 — \"Inline approval micro-confirm + undo\" (assignee: amanda).
